highlights.description: What a tool built around deployforge kept writing for itself is now deployforge's: loading a data-only dump, a per-stack credential check that records what it finds, a firewall check, a recurring deploy runbook for each live stack, the pieces for a tool's own runbooks, and the fleet's pages

added.description: db import <app> <stack> <database> --file <dump> loads a data-only dump as the database's owner in one transaction, with FORCE row-level security lifted for the load, row counts printed and the transaction rolled back without --confirm; --replace OLD=NEW replaces text first, and Options.ImportHook adds a host tool's own replacements

credentials preflight <app> <stack> compares the stack's secret prefix with the registry: each credential present with its date and whether it is recorded, each missing, and each name no credential lists; --record, --include-planned and --require-recorded; package form preflight.Inspect

host ports <host> --admin-cidr <cidr>... checks a Lightsail instance's firewall: HTTPS open exactly to Cloudflare's ranges, SSH only to the admin addresses, nothing else; the fleet's hosts gain lightsailName and Options.HostPorts opens the client

Package runbookkit: remote quoting for ssh, install-from-console actions, permission lists sorted part by part, step needs derived from commands, SSH-agent and token inputs, and fixes for SSH timeouts, refused keys, a release script without its executable bit, missing values, missing credentials and missing tokens
deploy runbook --app <app> --stack <stack> mounts a live stack's recurring deploy runbook, with export; Options.RunbookTool and RunbookDir; package deployrunbook
fleet inventory and fleet format write the fleet's inventory page and the fleet document's format reference; package fleetpage

changed.description: The fleet document's schema adds hosts[].lightsailName; existing documents are unchanged

documentation.description: The README, and the databases, credentials, hosts, deploying, fleet-document and embedding guides describe the new commands, packages and options

highlights.description: deploy ship refuses a release script that is not executable in the commit it packages, and --dry-run packages and checks a release without deploying it
A failed deploy names the step it stopped at, and ship, release, rollback and status can write one JSON report
iam apply needs --confirm, and iam policy prints a stack's policy for review

added.description: A failed release or rollback carries the step it stopped at (unpack, install, validate, the self-check's stages, migrate, switch or health), whether the running release was kept or restored, and whether the migration stays applied

--format json on deploy ship, release, rollback and status: one JSON report on standard output with the phase that failed, the host's failure, the ledger entry and ship's snapshot; progress goes to standard error

deploy ship checks, in the commit it packages, that the release script is executable (git mode 100755) and stops with the git update-index --chmod=+x fix when it is not; a shell script beside it that is not executable is reported as a warning
deploy ship --dry-run packages and checks the release, then stops: nothing is snapshotted, deployed or recorded
cli.Options.ReleaseEnv and ship.Options.Env give release scripts extra environment, for scripts at older tags that read other names; release package accepts --sites as an older name of --fleet
iam policy prints one stack's policy document for review, with --account, reading no AWS account
cloudflare-ips refreshes the committed Cloudflare ranges from the published lists, and --check fails when this build's ranges are out of date

changed.description: iam apply needs --confirm: without it, it shows the plan, changes nothing and says to run again with --confirm
For an app behind cloudflare, validate refuses a host name more than one label under its domain, which the zone's certificates do not cover

dependencies.description: Requires credforge v0.11.1, so the deploy preflight never counts a credential needed only during a rotation as missing

documentation.description: Migrations a rollback survives, and the JSON reports
The release script check, dry runs, iam policy and --confirm, cloudflare-ips, ReleaseEnv and the one-label host rule

highlights.description: The first release: deploy Go apps to your own Linux hosts with release archives, systemd and Caddy, a ledger, the edge, databases and credentials, from one fleet document

added.description: The fleet document: hosts (an address, or one from a Pulumi output), a port range, apps with named stacks, per-stack databases, limits and status, app labels, the database server and the credential registry, validated with every problem reported, and its JSON Schema

Releases from a clean, tagged, pushed commit, with the revision and checksum; local builds from local commits with upstream Go modules through a generated go.work and npm packages packed with pnpm, every input named in the archive and the ledger

Deploys over SSH with no agent on the host: unpack, install with backup, validate, migrate, an atomic switch, readiness on every host name, restore on failure, pruning; a deploy lock and an on-host audit log; deploy ship, release, rollback, unlock, status and unpushed
A ledger of every deploy and rollback per stack, with record, show, current and import from another tool's ledger
Hooks around packaging, deploy and rollback, and on failure, with no secret value in their environment
The host: systemd units with a hardening sandbox and limits, an idempotent host-setup script, a Caddyfile per host validated on the host before it is reloaded, and next-port

The edge: zones checked against their name servers, the security baseline through Cloudflare's API as plan, apply and verify, origin certificates made on the host and signed by Cloudflare, and a minimum TLS check from outside

Databases: owner and app roles with connection limits and SCRAM verifiers, their passwords in the parameter store; snapshots before a primary stack's deploy and on demand; copies between servers with row counts compared, and promotion of the new server's parameters

Credentials: the credential registry the fleet names, with systemspec-credential's commands and credforge's check, generate, install, review and setup; an HTML page per stack; a check before ship that every secret under the stack's prefix exists
Access: an IAM policy and an operators' group per stack's parameter-store prefix, as plan, apply and verify
Every capability as a Go package, and the Cobra command tree mountable under a host tool's command
